security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code spans, JavaScript examples, and official Firebase documentation links. Four Firebase CLI setup commands are confirmed medium-risk because they install or run latest tooling and may change local or project state; no prompt injection or malicious intent was found.

remediation.suggestion: Recommend a pinned Firebase CLI version and require user approval before global npm installation.

remediation.issue: Automatic npx execution with latest tooling
remediation.suggestion: Remove automatic -y usage or require confirmation before running npx commands that access Firebase projects.
State that firebase init can modify local files and enable services, then run it only after explicit user approval.

The skill instructs running npm install -g firebase@latest, which fetches mutable network code and changes global tooling state. This is legitimate setup guidance but still requires user approval.

The npx -y firebase-tools@latest command executes network-fetched tooling without an interactive package prompt. It can access authenticated Firebase project metadata, so it should not run automatically.
The npx -y firebase-tools@latest apps:list command executes remote package code and queries Firebase app metadata. This is a real external command risk even though the intent is administrative setup.
The npx firebase init command can modify local project files and enable Firebase AI Logic services. It is legitimate, but an agent should require explicit user confirmation before running it.

content.user_title: Integrate Firebase AI Logic in Web Apps
content.value_statement: Adding Gemini to a Firebase app can be confusing across setup, model choices, and security controls. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Firebase AI Logic setup and production checks.
actual_capabilities: Guides Firebase AI Logic initialization for web applications using the Firebase Web SDK.
Explains when to use the Gemini Developer API or Vertex AI Gemini API.
Provides patterns for text generation, chat sessions, streaming responses, and multimodal input.
Covers structured output, image generation, and hybrid on-device inference concepts.
Highlights production safeguards such as App Check and Remote Config for model names.
limitations: Focuses on Firebase AI Logic basics, with the strongest examples for web applications.
Does not replace official Firebase pricing, quota, or billing documentation.
Some setup commands can modify local or Firebase project state and need user approval.
Does not audit generated application code for privacy, policy, or prompt safety risks.

use_cases.title: Add Gemini to a Web App
use_cases.description: Set up Firebase AI Logic and call Gemini models from an existing Firebase web application.

use_cases.title: Plan Production AI Controls
use_cases.description: Apply App Check, model selection guidance, and Remote Config recommendations before launch.

use_cases.title: Prototype Multimodal Features
use_cases.description: Design chat, streaming, image input, and structured output flows for a product experiment.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Firebase AI Logic App
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me add Firebase AI Logic to my web app. Explain the required Firebase setup and ask before running any commands.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Text Generation Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a plan for a Firebase AI Logic text generation feature in my web app. Include initialization, model choice, and error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Design Multimodal and Streaming UX
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design Firebase AI Logic support for image input and streaming responses. Include user experience and file size considerations.

prompt_templates.title: Review Production Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Firebase AI Logic implementation for production readiness. Check App Check, Remote Config, model selection, billing, and security risks.

output_examples.input: I need to add Gemini text responses to a Firebase web app.
output_examples.output: The skill would outline Firebase app initialization, Firebase AI Logic setup, model selection, a text generation flow, and approval points for CLI commands.

output_examples.input: I want users to upload images and receive model analysis.
output_examples.output: The skill would describe supported multimodal inputs, browser file handling, size limits, Cloud Storage options, and response handling patterns.

output_examples.input: I am preparing a Firebase AI feature for launch.
output_examples.output: The skill would check App Check, billing plan needs, Remote Config model management, provider choice, and user consent for sensitive data.

best_practices: Ask for user approval before running Firebase CLI commands or changing project settings.
Enable Firebase App Check before exposing AI features to real users.
Use Remote Config for model names when production updates need fast rollback.
anti_patterns: Do not run latest npm or npx Firebase tooling without user confirmation.
Do not hardcode model names in production when Remote Config can manage changes.
Do not send large media inline when Cloud Storage references are more reliable.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps add Firebase AI Logic and Gemini model features to Firebase web applications.

faq.question: Does it support Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Can it choose between Gemini API providers?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains the Gemini Developer API and Vertex AI Gemini API selection guidance.

faq.question: Does it include security guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends Firebase App Check and cautions around CLI commands that change project state.

faq.question: Can it create multimodal AI features?
faq.answer: It provides guidance for image, audio, video, and PDF inputs through Firebase AI Logic patterns.

faq.question: Is it a complete Firebase reference?
faq.answer: No. It is focused on Firebase AI Logic basics and should be paired with official Firebase documentation.
